clauses.reason: Paragraph 1 provides that the named departments, agencies, the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations in the District of Columbia "shall be closed all day on" "Tuesday, December 24,1940" and that employees shall be excused from duty on that day, subject to the stated exceptions. The command is confined to that single calendar day, so it was exhausted by its own terms when that day ended; the end is recorded as December 24, 1940 inclusive, and the exclusive reading (ending when December 24 begins) is the alternative. The surviving consequence (excused absence) is an accrued effect, not a continuing command. No later instrument in the held record revokes, extends or amends it.

Paragraph 2 directs that the order be published in the Federal Register (the held text: "This order shall be published in the" Federal Register). That one-time direction was performed when the order appeared in the Federal Register issue headed "Washington, Wednesday, December 18, 1940" (5 FR 5143, filed December 17, 1940), which is the held source of the date. The clause had no further content after publication, so it ended on December 18, 1940, earlier than clause 1.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8613 of December 16, 1940 (5 FR 5143, Federal Register issue of December 18, 1940) closed executive departments and agencies in the District of Columbia and excused federal employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 1940, and directed its own publication in the Federal Register. Both clauses were spent by their own terms: clause 2 was performed when the order was published in the Federal Register issue dated December 18, 1940 (the filing line reads December 17, 1940), and clause 1 applied to the single calendar day December 24, 1940 and had no further subject after that day. The end date for clause 1 is recorded as December 24, 1940 inclusive (the order runs through that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when December 24 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No instrument held in the repository revokes, extends or amends the order. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription.

savings.reason: The excusal from duty on December 24, 1940 accrued to employees on that day. That consequence is a surviving effect of the executed closure, not a continuing command of Executive Order 8613; the order has no savings clause and the held searches show no later instrument touching it.
